engagement_title: Milepost Driving Academy learner guide refresh: cut eight dash filmed scenario takes into listenable phone clips and one vertical, bring six road stills shot across a changing Saturday to one house daylight, triage a photographed glyph sheet against a photographed roadside sign, and merge the printed learner guide out of the academy's own handout
vertical: Driver education and road safety training. An accredited academy running in car lessons and a classroom course, Burlington, Vermont
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post for a driving education content system quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, a driver education brand wanting a library of clean, mobile first explainer shorts on lane changes, turns, roundabouts, parking, merging, four way stops and hazard recognition, plus reusable branded templates and vector illustration. The literal ask in that post is from scratch After Effects two dimensional motion graphics animation, which is squarely on the connector's not available list (no text to image, no vector authoring, no After Effects timeline, no compositing), so the ledger's own note concedes the job has to be honestly re cast to the in scope production work this exact system needs. That is what this commission is: the same academy, the same eight scenarios, the same mobile first distribution, but built from what a small academy actually has, which is an instructor with a dash mount, a Saturday of photographs, a photographed sheet of the sign shapes their first designer drew, and the printer's file for the guide they hand every learner. The real post named no school, so the line is laundered to the fictional Milepost Driving Academy. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the recast honest, because a bare press PDF now becomes a live merge template headlessly and HTML authoring yields a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes.
client_one_liner: Our senior instructor filmed the eight scenarios off his dash and photographed the roads on a Saturday that started in fog and ended in low sun, and the printed guide we hand every learner still says two thousand nineteen on the back of it.
client_brief:
Milepost Driving Academy, the learner guide refresh

We are an accredited academy in Vermont. Two instructors, about sixty learners a term, mostly sixteen to nineteen with a steady number of adults who never got round to it. Lessons are sixty dollars an hour and our reputation is that we are calm and thorough. Everything a learner sees from us is from two thousand nineteen and it looks it, so we want the whole set rebuilt this autumn out of what we already have.

Our senior instructor drove the eight scenarios we teach and filmed them from a mount on the dash: lane changes, right turns, left turns across traffic, a roundabout, parallel parking, merging, a four way stop and hazard recognition. He narrated as he drove, in the car, with the engine running and the window cracked. The clips are for a phone, short, one idea each, and they need to be listenable rather than broadcast. One of them should exist tall as well, for stories.

He photographed the same roads on one Saturday that started in fog and ended in low sun. Six of those are the reference pictures for the guide, and they have to look like one day, because a learner comparing two of them should be reading the road and not the weather. There is no modern roundabout near us that photographs well, so if you have to buy one picture, buy one.

We use a small set of simplified sign shapes throughout the guide. Those only exist on a sheet our first designer printed, and what we have is a photograph of that sheet. We also want the real sign on the county road on its own, so it can sit on a coloured page.

The printed guide is one scenario to a page. We have the printer's file from two thousand nineteen and a spreadsheet of the copy as our instructors have rewritten it. We would also like something we can post alongside each clip.

Nothing stylised, please. A learner has to be certain what they are looking at, and so does a parent paying for the course.
price_band_and_audience: A sixty dollar per hour accredited lesson package, learners sixteen to nineteen plus adult beginners, with the purchase decision usually made by a parent. The band is load bearing. This is not a lifestyle brand and it is not a budget one: the work has to read as calm, neutral, legible and accountable, with signs unambiguous, daylight consistent, type plain and generously set, and no colour treatment that a nervous learner or a cautious parent could read as styling over substance. The same eight scenarios for a thirty dollar app subscription would correctly be bright, high contrast, fast cut and heavily captioned, and shipping that here reads as a phone game rather than as an accredited school. Push the other way into cinematic grading, moody low sun and a hero treatment of the car and it becomes a driving experience brand at two hundred dollars an hour, which misprices the lesson and, worse, makes a road picture harder to read. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,000 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Driver education and road safety training (accredited in car and classroom academy)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2009 in Burlington, Vermont. Small: two instructors, roughly sixty learners a term.
brand_identity.about: Milepost is an accredited driving academy in Vermont running in car lessons and a classroom course. Our reputation is that we are calm and thorough, and every learner leaves certain about what they are looking at. Everything we make has to earn the trust of a nervous learner and the parent paying for the course.
brand_identity.audience: Learners sixteen to nineteen plus adult beginners, with the purchase decision usually made by a parent. People who want reassurance that the school is careful and legitimate.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid, accredited and dependable. Sixty dollars an hour. Not a budget app, not a premium driving experience brand.
brand_identity.typography: A plain, highly legible system: a clear humanist sans for titles and step lists, set generously, with a neutral companion for call outs and captions. Legibility at small size in a printed guide and on a phone is the whole criterion. Nothing expressive or condensed.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, instructive, reassuring. One idea at a time, numbered where it helps, no slang and no drama. Speaks plainly to a beginner and to the parent reading over their shoulder.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Everything a learner currently sees from us dates to 2019 and looks it. The printer holds the press file for the guide, but the source files for our simplified sign shapes are gone: they only survive as a photograph of a sheet our first designer printed and taped to the wall, so those glyphs have to be recovered from that. No brand typeface was ever locked, so the type system is open for you to set to our legibility standard.
brand_identity.values: Certainty over style. A learner and a parent must always be sure what they are looking at. Nothing stylised, nothing that reads as styling over substance, consistency that shows the school is careful.

assets_supplied.name: milepost_scenario_takes/ (8 clips, dash mounted, narrated in car)
assets_supplied.kind: Single camera dash mount footage of the eight taught scenarios, driven and narrated in one Saturday morning session by the senior instructor.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The eight scenarios as he drove them. He narrates as he goes, so the words are on the clip already."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the eight are the same junction filmed on two passes in different lanes and one taught scenario has no take at all, which no filename, duration or the client's own list reveals. Several takes also carry a long approach with the manoeuvre itself in the last seconds, and two were recorded before the mount was upgraded so they are seven hundred and twenty lines tall while the rest are ten eighty.

assets_supplied.name: milepost_road_stills/ (6 frames, one Saturday, fog to low sun)
assets_supplied.kind: Reference photographs of the same roads, shot handheld and through the windscreen across a single day whose weather changed completely.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six reference roads, all one Saturday. They need to look like one day."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two were shot straight into the low sun and their skies are clipped to paper with no data behind them, so a highlight recovery on those two returns a picture that has not changed while reporting success, and the readout is that nothing moved. Two others were shot through the windscreen and carry a faint dashboard reflection and a polariser band across the sky, and one is off level.

assets_supplied.name: milepost_glyph_sheet.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of a printed sheet, taped to a wall, carrying the academy's small set of simplified sign shapes drawn by their first designer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our simplified sign shapes. This sheet is the only place they exist now."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a photograph of a printed sheet on a wall rather than a flat scan, so a prompt naming the sheet returns the paper and the tape rather than the drawn shapes, and the ink runs close to the paper in the corner the room light does not reach. The yield glyph is an enclosed outline whose interior a background knockout cannot punch, so that route hands back a filled triangle that looks like a successful cutout.

assets_supplied.name: milepost_county_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the real roadside sign on the county road, taken from the verge on a flat overcast morning.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The real sign on the county road. We want it on its own so it can sit on a coloured page."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sign face is retro reflective and the overcast sky behind it that morning sits at close to the same brightness, so a one call knockout returns something that looks complete and correct at preview scale while biting the top edge of the sign and the shadow side of the post. Nothing in the response says so and the bite only shows at full resolution against a colour.

assets_supplied.name: milepost_guide_2019.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the academy's printer produced for the learner guide in 2019, one scenario to a page, with a photograph well, a title, a numbered steps block and a short call out.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The printer's file for the guide. One scenario per page, same as we hand out now."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The steps block is a fixed measure frame sized around the shortest scenario in the 2019 copy, and a longer record does not push it, spill it or overset it visibly: the text simply stops rendering at the trim edge, with no warning in the merge response and no error anywhere. The photograph well and the steps block also sit closer together in the artwork than the printed page suggests.

assets_supplied.name: milepost_copy_2026.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain data: the eight scenarios with their titles, numbered step lists, call outs and the filename each expects for its photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as our two instructors have rewritten it this year. The wording is theirs."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The step lists are wildly uneven, from three lines to eleven, because two instructors wrote them separately and neither was writing to a measure. The roundabout row names a photograph filename that does not exist in anything the academy supplied.

acceptance_bar: Each scenario clip actually shows the manoeuvre it is named for, and shows it long enough to be understood. A clip that is the correct length and consists of an approach is a failed deliverable.
Every taught scenario is accounted for. A scenario that cannot be delivered from the material supplied is named, with what is missing, not quietly filled with something adjacent.
The narration is listenable end to end on a phone speaker, without the instructor sounding processed.

No delivered video is taller or wider than the source it came from, and no delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions. Anything that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The six road stills read as one day. One white point, one sky treatment, one contrast. A frame that cannot be brought to the day is named in the note rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The licensed roundabout picture sits inside the same day as the six, judged beside them at full size rather than as a thumbnail.
The signs are unambiguous. Nothing in the grade or the treatment makes a sign face harder to read than it is on the road.

The simplified glyphs are placeable artwork rather than pictures of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and the enclosed shapes genuinely open rather than filled.
The county sign cut out holds its edge at full resolution against a colour, including the top edge and the shadow side of the post.

The printed guide carries one scenario per page with the complete step list for every scenario visible inside the page, page count equal to row count, and each scenario's own photograph on its own page.
The posted cards sit in ONE editable working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the self contained source is delivered alongside it.

One type system across the guide and the cards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used, and the note stating per photograph and per clip what was applied and what could not be.

adobe_surfaces.role: The headline deliverable. Eight long dash takes are indexed rather than watched, which is also the only way the material is reconciled against the eight taught scenarios, then shortened rather than assembled, because the cutter only removes and chooses its own spans. The in car narration is lifted out of engine and wind noise without being turned into a studio voice, and the one vertical is reached by reframing without ever enlarging, which is the constraint that decides which take can supply it.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision, and the triage at the centre of the job. It fixes one house daylight off the best frame and brings six frames shot from fog to low sun toward it one call at a time, confines corrections where a whole frame move would take a sign face or a sky the wrong way, and then takes two superficially similar photographed inputs down deliberately opposite routes: the drawn glyph sheet to ink level selection and a trace, the photographed roadside sign to a transparent cutout inspected at full resolution.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign, template archaeology and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and again as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The printed learner guide, one scenario to a page at genuine print resolution, built by reverse engineering the printer's own 2019 press PDF because no native InDesign file exists. The IDML round trip is the only honest channel for what the converted document really contains and what measure each frame really holds, the photograph column has to bind per row against images the agent produced itself, and the proofs have to be rendered on the route that actually yields print resolution.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The cards the academy posts alongside each clip, as one native editable document carrying roots at more than one canvas size, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. The recovered glyphs go in as inline SVG so they stay editable vector at any size, every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and family and weight are declared per element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across the printed guide and the posted cards. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on calm, accountable and legible at small size for a teenage learner and a paying parent rather than on anything expressive. Numeric weights are non standard per family, every name has to be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one picture the academy cannot shoot, a modern roundabout, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative technology candidates excluded, which then has to be brought into the same Saturday as the six. The Boards half persists the reference set the two instructors sign off from, placed within the per call placement cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The guide is a genuine one record per page run and belongs in the merge; the posted cards are designed one offs and belong in authored HTML because the academy will change them per term. The brief pins both destinations.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed tier that gates the export.

trajectory.action: Upload the eight takes, the six stills, the glyph sheet, the county sign frame, the printer PDF and the copy data, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: The manifest has to survive a run with two families of images that must never be confused, so it is keyed by role rather than by filename.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Index all eight takes and reconcile what the material actually contains against the eight taught scenarios: which manoeuvre each take really shows, where in each take it happens, and whether every scenario is present.
trajectory.judgement: Filenames are the instructor's, written at the roadside. The content is the only thing that settles what each take is, and reading the takes against the scenario list is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A take to scenario reconciliation with the manoeuvre located inside each take.

trajectory.action: Cut each usable take down to a phone length clip, one idea each, accepting that the tool only shortens and chooses its own spans.
trajectory.judgement: There is no assembly and no timeline. The only lever is the target length per take, and it is a different decision for a take with a thirty second approach than for one that starts at the junction.
trajectory.produces: A set of short scenario clips with the chosen length recorded per take.

trajectory.action: Clean the in car narration so it is listenable without turning the instructor into a studio voice.
trajectory.judgement: Engine, wind and tyre noise are the environment the lesson happens in. The academy asked for listenable, not broadcast, and a clip in which the road has gone silent under a processed voice reads as a re recording rather than as a lesson.
trajectory.produces: Cleaned narration judged against the untreated original.

trajectory.action: Produce the one vertical by reframing the chosen clip for stories, without enlarging anything.
trajectory.judgement: A wide source reframed tall keeps its height and loses its width, so which take can supply the vertical is decided by what its source height actually is, and by where the road and the manoeuvre sit across the frame.
trajectory.produces: A vertical clip at or below its source height, with the choice of take and the reframe decision recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview the six road stills, the glyph sheet and the county sign frame and triage them: which stills are windscreen shots, which are into the sun, which is off level, and which of the two sign inputs is drawn artwork and which is a photographed object.
trajectory.judgement: The two sign inputs look alike as files and need opposite treatments. Deciding that from the filenames is guessing; deciding it from the pictures is the job.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note naming route per input.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a horizon that leans is the first thing a learner notices in a road picture.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house daylight off the best lit frame and bring each of the six toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is one day, not six good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames that run from fog to low sun; the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by six different routes, and decide where a frame stops being worth saving.
trajectory.produces: Six road masters on one house daylight with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong: the dashboard reflection, the polariser band, and anything that would make a sign face harder to read.
trajectory.judgement: Selection wording is the gate, and legibility outranks consistency here. A frame brought perfectly to the day at the cost of a readable sign has failed the actual purpose of the picture.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have cost a sign or muddied a sky.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a modern roundabout, filter to photography, exclude generative technology results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it into the same house daylight.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the day, not the prettiest thumbnail, and remember the thumbnail is not the picture. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale roundabout frame graded toward the set.

trajectory.action: Take the two sign inputs down their separate routes: the glyph sheet through an ink level selection naming the drawn shapes' own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop, a trace, a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas path removed; the county sign through a transparent knockout inspected at full resolution against a colour.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: which input is artwork and which is an object, how to word each selection so it takes the ink and not the paper, and that a background knockout is the wrong instrument on an enclosed glyph interior.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent glyph set plus a transparent cutout of the real sign.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against an accredited school, a teenage learner and a paying parent. Legibility at small size in a printed guide is the criterion, not personality.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.surface: InDesign, template archaeology and data merge
trajectory.action: Convert the printer's 2019 press PDF, round trip it to IDML and read the real frame inventory and the real measure of each frame, reconstruct the true story text, compute every offset from that string, build and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then round trip again and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed guide looks like says nothing about what the converted document exposes, and the readout of a story is not the story. Both the validator and the prepare step report success on a mapping that has already lost fields, so the only evidence of a complete template is finding the placeholders in the document itself.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders and frame measures are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Merge the scenario records one to a page with each scenario's own prepared photograph bound per row, deliver as one press file in the copy's row order, and render proofs at genuine print resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Order and identity are the deliverable. The route that preserves row order is not the route that produces the fastest proofs, the photograph column binds only in one exact shape, and print resolution comes from the render rather than from the merge.
trajectory.produces: One press file at one scenario per page plus print resolution proofs, each scenario carrying its own photograph.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with roots at more than one canvas size, inline every photograph as image data, place the glyphs as inline SVG inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how plainly a scenario can be stated on a card that a nervous learner will read on a phone.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the posted card set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the others.

trajectory.action: Create the reference board, add the graded stills, the licensed frame and the sign artwork within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is a partial success, and vector artwork is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to name every scenario that could not be delivered and why.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a shortened clip still contains the manoeuvre it is named for. The cutter only removes and chooses its own spans, so which part of a several minute dash take survives is not the agent's decision. Several of these takes carry a long approach with the manoeuvre itself in the last seconds, and which ones do is a property of how the instructor drove that morning rather than of anything in the file. The cut returns a clean, correctly sized clip either way, and a clip that is entirely a calm approach up to a junction looks exactly like a correct result until somebody watches it for the thing it is supposed to teach.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering dodges it and no parameter prevents it, because span selection belongs to the tool and there is no trim to a timestamp available here; indexing first tells the agent where the manoeuvre sits, which is precisely why the mismatch is visible after the cut and not before it. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the clips should be short, one idea each, and listenable, which is a specification, not a disclosure about where in each take the idea happens. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different route per take: cut to a different target length so a different span survives, or supply that scenario from the second pass of the junction that was filmed twice, or declare the scenario undeliverable from this material and say so, which then changes what the printed guide's page for that scenario can carry.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the affected takes at different lengths and inspect each result against the manoeuvre it is named for, re assign at least one scenario to a different source, re decide which take can supply the vertical, and carry the scenario that has no usable take through into the guide's page plan and into the handover as a named gap.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A library of correctly sized, correctly named scenario clips in which the roundabout clip never reaches the roundabout, published by an accredited school to teenagers learning to drive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two into the sun frames can be brought to the day at all. They look recoverable: bright sky, strong subject, the kind of frame a highlight recovery is for. Their skies are clipped to paper with nothing behind them, so pulling highlights returns an image that is indistinguishable from the input, and the readout is that nothing moved. There is no measurement available anywhere in this family, no histogram and no readout of what was clipped, so the state of the highlight data is not knowable from the file, from the preview, or from the parameters; it is knowable only by applying the move and looking at what came back.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, since the recovery has to be attempted before its result exists, and no parameter prevents it, since the data is simply absent. Doing it right the first time would require knowing in advance which two of six frames are clipped, which nothing reports. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the Saturday started in fog and ended in low sun and that the six must look like one day, which is the client describing the shoot and stating the target, not warning that two frames are unrecoverable. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different treatment for those frames: build the correction from below rather than from above, or change the crop so the dead sky is not in the picture, which then changes the crop logic the other four have to agree with, or name the frame as unrecoverable and take that scenario's picture from elsewhere.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the correction route for the affected frames, re decide the crop logic for all six so they still agree, re judge the licensed roundabout frame against a set that has now moved, and carry any frame that cannot be brought to the day into the handover as a named exclusion with what a reshoot would need.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A reference set in which two of six road pictures still carry a blown white sky and a different contrast from their neighbours, delivered as one consistent day, so a learner comparing two pages reads the weather instead of the road and the school's most visible claim, that it is thorough, is contradicted on the page.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every scenario's steps actually appear on its page. The steps frame in the printer's 2019 artwork is a fixed measure sized around the shortest scenario in the old copy, and the 2026 copy runs from three lines to eleven because two instructors wrote it separately. A record whose steps exceed the measure does not push the frame, does not spill and does not flag as overset anywhere in the merge response: the text simply stops rendering at the trim edge. The merge reports success, the page count is right, the photograph is bound correctly, and the page looks like a finished page. Which records overflow depends on the interaction between this copy and this frame's real measure, and neither is knowable until the merge is rendered and the pages are read.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because there is no autofit, no overset report and no way to interrogate a frame's capacity except by putting text in it and rendering. Reading the frame bounds in the round trip tells the agent the measure exists, not which of eight records will exceed it in practice. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the guide is one scenario to a page and that the wording is the instructors' own, which is a constraint on the copy, not a warning about the frame. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a decision the client has to be part of: shorten a step list the instructors wrote and the brief protects, re map the overflow into a second frame the round trip showed actually exists, or split that scenario across two pages, and each of those changes what the page and the merge look like.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read all eight rendered pages rather than the merge response, identify every record whose steps stop at trim, choose and justify a route per record, adjust the mapping or the copy accordingly, re prepare the template if the mapping changed, re merge, re render and re read every page.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A printed learner guide handed to sixty learners a term in which the longest and most cautious step lists, the ones for the hardest manoeuvres, end mid instruction at the edge of the page, on a product whose entire promise is that the school is thorough.

deliverables.name: Milepost scenario clip library and one vertical
deliverables.spec: A short phone clip per taught scenario, one idea each, in which the manoeuvre the clip is named for is actually shown and understandable, with the in car narration listenable end to end and still sounding like a car on a road. Plus one vertical version for stories at or below its source height. Every scenario accounted for: any that cannot be delivered from the supplied material is named with what is missing, not filled with something adjacent.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion work, which are raster work, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Whether the eight files are the eight scenarios. The academy believes they are; only the content can settle it, and how to report a gap honestly is part of the job.
The target length per take, which is the only lever over an automatic cut and is a different decision for a take with a long approach than for one that starts at the junction.
Which take can supply the vertical, given that two of the eight were recorded at a lower height and nothing may be enlarged.
How much road noise to leave under the narration, since the environment is the lesson and a silent road reads as a re recording.
Whether the six stills are one day. Laid in a row is the only place that can be settled, and how far to push a fog frame before it stops being worth saving.
Whether to bring a frame perfectly to the day at the cost of a readable sign, which is the one trade this client cannot accept.

Which of the two sign inputs is drawn artwork and which is a photographed object, and therefore which gets traced and which gets cut out. Getting this backwards yields a plausible looking result from either tool.

Selection wording on the glyph sheet: naming the sheet takes the paper and the tape, naming the drawn shapes' own visual properties takes the ink, and a background knockout on an enclosed glyph interior is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether a licensed roundabout frame joins the day the six live in or reads as bought, judged at full size rather than from the thumbnail.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged on legibility at small size for a teenage learner and a paying parent, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How plain the cards should be. At this band plainness is the design, and an energetic, high contrast, heavily captioned card is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns illustrations of roads and signs. IDENTITY: these are the academy's own eight taught scenarios filmed on their own county roads, their own instructor's narration, their own first designer's simplified glyphs recovered rather than reinvented, and the actual sign on the actual county road; a regenerated sign is a sign that does not exist, which in driver education is not a stylistic problem but a safety one. SPEC: the printer needs one scenario per page with page count equal to row count, every step list complete inside its page and each scenario's own photograph on its own page, plus proofs at genuine print resolution, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for, and every clip is a shortening of real footage that must never be enlarged. EDITABILITY: the cards are defined by being editable, since the academy revises the copy each term and its instructors rewrite the steps themselves. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: does this clip reach the roundabout, did this highlight recovery change anything at all, does this record's eleventh step exist on the page.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), six surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. PREMIERE: the four sanctioned video and audio tools are used strictly inside their verified envelope, media_summarize as the content index and reconciliation channel, video_create_quick_cut which only SHORTENS (never lengthens, never reorders, never trims to a timestamp), media_enhance_speech on narration, and video_resize which never enlarges. No frame extraction, no format conversion, no timeline assembly, and no deliverable depends on any capability outside those four. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The triage rests on live findings: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry (a card level mask of 154,926 px versus a 9,372 px ink mask on the same frame), remove_background returning a SOLID OPAQUE DISC on an enclosed ring interior (118,823 opaque px where a true knockout is about 18,000), and remove_background collapsing where subject and ground share value. Alpha survives crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial alpha pixels preserved), so the sign cutout is real, and the missing viewBox plus the opaque path zero are documented, which is exactly the hygiene the acceptance bar scores. INDESIGN: the full archaeology chain is verified end to end from a bare press PDF through convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt and prepare_indd_merge_template to a live template, with one record per page confirmed for PDF output (page count equals row count, verified at three rows), per row image binding confirmed visually through an at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles, and true 300 dpi raster confirmed only via document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution is silently ignored in the merge (2550 x 3300 at density 300 verified). Row order is taken through the PDF and createSeparateFiles routes, which are the routes verified correct, never through multi record raster output, which came back REVERSED. The truncation checkpoint rests on the frame measure being real and fixed in a PDF derived template and on there being no overset report anywhere in the response surface. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, orientation never passed (it always returns zero hits), contentType filtering and isGenTech exclusion verified, license returned a real 7360 x 4912 JPEG, renditionURL confirmed to be only a 240 px thumbnail so the true colour of a licensed frame exists only after the full resolution download, and boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call where 201 means partial. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html and no photograph is ever left as a URL. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. AVOIDED: no video_render, video_render_frame or video_metadata, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no variable QR, no bleed claim on a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
